newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-CAF SHIFT ANNIVERSARY FESTIVAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAF SHIFT ANNIVERSARY FESTIVAL.

text.p: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) is to switch its 40th anniversary celebrations in August from Ethiopia to Egypt because of political problems.

CAF press officer Viken Djizmedjian said on Monday the move had been made because "the Ethiopians were not ready to host it". But other sources said the confederation had encountered difficulties with the Ethiopian government.
Ethiopia was chosen because it is one of the four founding members of CAF and to pay homage to former CAF president Ydnekatchew Tessema.
Tessema, who died 10 years ago, is seen as the father of modern African football and the man responsible for setting in motion the development of the sport on the African continent.
Current CAF president Issa Hayatou had planned to lay a wreath on the grave of Tessema in Addis Ababa.

But the Ethiopian government, who came to power after a long-standing civil war, see Tessema as an active member of past regimes, who are held responsible for the deaths of hundreds of thousands of Ethiopians.
Tessema, a founding member of CAF in 1957, served in various government capacities from 1968 to 1981, including an eight-year stint as a deputy sports minister.
CAF will now host the festival at its Cairo headquarters in "the second half of August," said Djizmedjian.
